subject: Post-deploy: v5 modelpack causing p95/p99 spikes & 5xx increase
messages:
From: Sam Helsey <sam.helsey@insituhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: support+insitu@insituhealth.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-deploy: v5 modelpack causing p95/p99 spikes & 5xx increase

Jordan —

We just finished the v5 modelpack + QP-7 quantization rollout on our production endpoint (region: us-west-2) and immediately saw p95/p99 latency jump ~2.1x and a spike in 5xx rates from 0.2% to ~3.6%. Throughput dropped about 18% under identical load. I attached a short CSV with p99 by minute and a filtered request log showing the most common prompt shapes.

From our QA sampling, a subset of customer prompts also show degraded answer completeness — truncation/shorter outputs — which aligns with the quant changes. This is hitting our SLAs and we're getting customer escalations.

Could you confirm whether Redwood enabled the new runtime kernel selection for the v5 modelpack, and whether QP-7 is behaving as a strict int8 profile? We need either an immediate fallback (v4a) or a mitigation plan within the next 3 hours.

Attachments: p99_latency_report.csv, sample_request_log.txt, slo_errors_snapshot.json

Requesting an urgent bridge at 11:00 PT if we can.

— Sam Helsey
CTO, Insitu Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Helsey <sam.helsey@insituhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-deploy: v5 modelpack causing p95/p99 spikes & 5xx increase

Sam — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We're treating this as high priority. Quick summary of immediate actions we are initiating now: 

- Rolling an automatic fallback to your pinned variant v4a for production traffic within the next 30 minutes (will keep a small canary on v5 for telemetry).
- Temporarily disabling the QP-7 quantization profile for v5 (we'll serve a non-quantized or QP-5 variant while we investigate).
- Increasing your dedicated pool concurrency by +20% to absorb transient backpressure.

I asked Ben (runtime lead) and Irene (SRE) to join the bridge and run a quick root-cause triage. We'll share a short incident timeline and next steps on the bridge. Please confirm the 11:00 PT bridge and if you want Redwood to proceed with a full rollback vs. staged fallback.

Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 08:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-deploy: v5 modelpack causing p95/p99 spikes & 5xx increase

Looping in more detail on what I'm seeing from the runtime side: 

- Telemetry (shared link above) shows a sharp displacement in token-generation time once kv-cache hit ratios drop for long-context prompts; v5's attention kernel path is switching to a fallback code path for sequences >1024 tokens and that path currently has a slower per-token kernel with QP-7.
- QP-7 appears to alter chunking behavior for attention blocks; combined with longer average sequence lengths from Insitu's workload, we're seeing more frequent small-batch stalls.
- Error traces are dominated by OOM-retries followed by 5xx for overloaded pods and a small increase in model token truncation.

Immediate recommendation (to Jordan & Irene): execute the rollback_playbook_v2: disable QP-7 flag, force-evict v5 pods from production ring, and shift traffic to v4a. We can keep a 2% shadow of v5 with QP-5 for diagnostics.

I'll be on the bridge and will post the exact runbook steps and ETA (target mitigation < 45m). — Ben
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Helsey <sam.helsey@insituhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-deploy: v5 modelpack causing p95/p99 spikes & 5xx increase

Adding a quick leadership note: I'm flagging this for the executive on-call loop in case we need SLA credits or an enterprise remediation plan. Marissa — can you please join the bridge and help coordinate any commercial communications?

For the bridge: join via https://redwood.zoom.us/j/9382211 (pw: RH-bridge).

Irene Choi
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Helsey <sam.helsey@insituhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-deploy: v5 modelpack causing p95/p99 spikes & 5xx increase

Thanks — we accepted the fallback to v4a at 09:12 PT and saw p95 drop back to near-baseline within ~20 minutes. Throughput is recovering; 5xx has gone down to ~0.4% but a small fraction of long-context prompts still show truncation artifacts (we believe those were processed on the canary v5 pods).

We appreciate the quick action. Two asks from our side: 
1) ETA on a postmortem that describes root cause and whether the QP-7 quant profile is still recommended for our workload.
2) A short-term configuration suggestion to avoid this pattern repeating (we noted that our average sequence length distribution skews longer than the training benchmarks).

— Sam
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Helsey <sam.helsey@insituhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 07:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-deploy: v5 modelpack causing p95/p99 spikes & 5xx increase

Sam — follow-up and next steps: 

- Short incident summary: v5 + QP-7 introduced an attention-kernel path that increases per-token latency for sequences above 1k tokens. Combined with Insitu's longer prompt distribution this pushed more requests into a slower code path and increased OOM-retries. (Ben and engineering will publish full telemetry + stack traces in the postmortem.)
- Immediate mitigation already executed: fallback to v4a, QP-7 disabled for your account, dedicated pool concurrency increased.
- Short-term config suggestions: pin quant profile to QP-5 or disable quantization for the long-context routing class; set a token-length based route to ensure long-context requests hit nodes with the high-memory kernel. We'll provide an ops snippet to implement this.
- Deliverables: 1) 24-hour postmortem (Ben & Eng) with timeline and root cause, 2) a configuration playbook tailored to your token-length profile, 3) one-week follow-up to validate stability.

Related links: https://console.redwood.example.com/tickets/REDW-22418 (incident ticket), Drive report attached.

We'll keep you updated and assign a technical owner for the follow-up work. Thanks again for escalating quickly — apologies for the disruption.

Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
